function.mechanism: Hydrocolloid that increases viscosity and stabilizes food systems; largely not digested intact and fermented in the gut.
common_food_categories: foods for infants and young children
foods for special medical purposes (including anti-regurgitation formulas)

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 concluded no need for a numerical ADI for the general population; EFSA 2023 used a 1,400 mg/kg bw/day reference point with an MoE approach for infant/FSMP scenarios.

efsa.key_finding: No general-population safety concern at refined exposure, but infant FSMP scenarios can yield MoE below 1 at maximum/high exposure levels.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (database shows evaluations including 1981, 2016, and 2025).

concerns.summary: EFSA 2023 identified a reference point of 1,400 mg/kg bw/day based on reduced blood zinc in neonatal piglets; high infant FSMP exposure scenarios produced MoE below 1.
JECFA 2025 considered intestinal microbiota disruption and concluded no concern at assessed uses, while still identifying potential risk at 10,000 mg/L infant formula via MoE.
A 2025 case report suggests carob-bean-gum-thickened formula may impair levothyroxine absorption in congenital hypothyroidism.
EFSA follow-up mentions limited adverse reaction reporting, including rare allergy signal(s), with low event count.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no adverse effects at highest doses in 90-day and carcinogenicity rodent studies
EFSA 2017: no concern for genotoxicity or reproductive/developmental toxicity
Infant formula studies (2023 real-world, 2024 RCT) reported good tolerance and no major new safety signal

populations: infants below 16 weeks consuming FSMP at maximum/high use levels
infants above 16 weeks consuming FSMP at high (p95) exposure
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI is set; risk characterization is based on MoE to a 1,400 mg/kg bw/day reference point, and MoE can fall below 1 in high infant scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory acceptance is broad (EU authorized, US GRAS, JECFA ADI not specified), but EFSA and JECFA both identify scenario-dependent concern in infant special-medical-purpose uses at higher concentrations/exposures.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no numerical ADI needed for general population
EFSA 2023: RP 1,400 mg/kg bw/day and MoE below 1 in some infant scenarios
JECFA 2025: potential risk at 10,000 mg/L infant formula, low risk at lower concentrations
Recent infant clinical studies generally show good tolerance
